justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep the R6 base resource named `SubstanceSpecification` while clarifying its definition and preferred terminology, or retain a deprecated same-named base alias.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Avoids the root resourceType break at the cost of living with a less precise legacy name; an alias would add duplicate canonical resource names.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The goal of positioning the artifact as a substance definition is reasonable, but the identity break is not clearly necessary. The computable evidence shows the R4 resource name disappeared and `SubstanceDefinition` is the successor, yet the same domain goal could largely have been met by retaining the R4 resource identity and improving definitions, mappings, and conformance text.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base design would have kept `SubstanceSpecification` as the R6 resource type and canonical StructureDefinition while updating the description and internal model to reflect definition-oriented semantics. If HL7 wanted to introduce `SubstanceDefinition`, retaining `SubstanceSpecification` as a deprecated base alias would also reduce parser, routing, and reference breakage, though that alias approach risks two canonical names for the same concept.

justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain deprecated R4 property children while adding `type` and generalized `value[x]`, with required typing enforced by profiles or warnings during transition.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Improves compatibility but leaves duplicate property encodings, weaker base validation for untyped properties, and long-term implementation burden.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal appears reasonable: make each property typed and generalize value representations. A fully compatible base design would not cleanly meet that goal because R4 allowed untyped properties and used several old child elements with different semantics. The remaining less-breaking options are transitional and materially increase ambiguity.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: R6 could have preserved `property.code`, `amount[x]`, `category`, `parameters`, and `definingSubstance[x]` as deprecated fields while adding `property.type` and `property.value[x]`. That would preserve many R4 instances, including old quantity/string values, but it would create overlapping same-resource representations for the same fact and would not guarantee that all properties have a meaningful type unless stricter profiles rejected some legacy records.

justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep the old optional `relationship.relationship` and Range amount as deprecated alternatives while adding the R6 `type` and renamed fields.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves more R4 records but weakens the base guarantee that relationships are typed and leaves duplicate amount/name representations.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Requiring an interpretable relationship type and aligning references with the successor substance resource are reasonable R6 goals. Less-breaking choices exist, especially retaining the old name and `Range` choice, but they would preserve incomplete or ambiguous relationship records in the base model.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A transitional base design could have kept `relationship.relationship` optional as an alias for `type`, retained `amountRange`, and made required typing a profile rule or warning. That would reduce immediate invalidation of R4 data but would leave consumers handling two names for relationship type, more amount forms, and untyped relationships that R6 appears to be trying to avoid.

justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain the specialized companion reference elements and their target resource types as deprecated R6 content while introducing the simplified inline model.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Protects legacy substance detail but keeps a broad old companion-resource family in core and duplicates simplified R6 representations.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Consolidating the substance model is a plausible R6 design goal, and retaining all R4 companion targets would materially undermine that simplification. The break remains high-risk because referenced protein, polymer, nucleic-acid, reference-information, and source-material payloads can be important and no official map was available in the local inputs.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design would have kept `referenceInformation`, `nucleicAcid`, `polymer`, `protein`, and reference-style `sourceMaterial` as deprecated optional elements, with the old companion StructureDefinitions still valid as R6 targets. That is a real base-design alternative, not merely migration tooling, but it carries major long-term costs: implementers would need to support both the old specialized resource family and the newer simplified inline representation.

justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Allow both the old inline `Attachment` and the new `Reference(DocumentReference)` representation during a transition.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves inline payloads but creates duplicate retrieval/provenance patterns for structural representation files.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Normalizing structural files through `DocumentReference` and adding an explicit format element is a coherent R6 goal. A less-breaking choice could preserve inline attachments, but it would leave two competing ways to carry the same structural artifact and make consumers handle both inline and referenced document lifecycles.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: R6 could have retained `structure.representation.attachment` or made the document-bearing element a choice that accepted either `Attachment` or `Reference(DocumentReference)`. That would preserve R4 instances with embedded MOLFILE, image, or other data, but it would dilute the normalized document model and complicate provenance, access control, and retrieval behavior.

justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep molecular-weight `amount` optional with a warning/profile requirement and retain isotope details as a deprecated optional backbone.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves incomplete and isotope-rich R4 records but weakens base validation and keeps extra legacy structure.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Making molecular-weight entries quantitatively meaningful is reasonable, but the combined break is not fully justified by the local evidence. Requiring `amount` rejects historical records that carried method or type only, and removing isotope-specific content has no clear replacement in the supplied StructureDefinitions.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could have left `molecularWeight.amount` optional while adding a best-practice warning or profile requirement for complete records, and could have retained `structure.isotope` as deprecated content. This would not fully satisfy a strict base guarantee that every molecular weight has an amount, and it would preserve additional legacy complexity, so the alternative is only partial.

justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `status` non-modifier and rely on narrative guidance, preferred binding, or warning-level conformance guidance for retired records.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Avoids generated-code modifier churn but provides a weaker safety signal that implementations may ignore.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: This is not a hard instance validation break, but it is a real runtime/conformance change. The R6 goal of formally signaling that lifecycle status can affect safe use is reasonable, and a non-modifier alternative would be less disruptive but materially weaker.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: R6 could have retained the R4 non-modifier flag and documented that retired or inactive statuses require special handling. That base design would preserve older processor assumptions, but it would not give validators, generated models, or safety checks the explicit modifier signal that R6 uses for data that can change interpretation.

justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Use an extensible or preferred all-languages binding first, then tighten to required after legacy language codings can be mapped.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves local codings but weakens validation and reliable language-based processing.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Standardizing language tags is an interoperable and reasonable goal, and the element remains optional. The less-breaking alternative is real but materially weaker because R4 allowed arbitrary CodeableConcepts and a softer binding would continue to accept non-standard language identifiers.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: R6 could have introduced the all-languages value set with preferred or extensible strength, possibly with guidance to map legacy local language codes. That would preserve most populated R4 `name.language` instances, but it would not provide the same base conformance guarantee that language values are valid IETF language tags.

justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No less-breaking forward base design is needed because these are optional R6 additions, not R4-to-R6 invalidating changes.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The tradeoff is richer R6 expressivity versus lossy R6-to-R4 down-conversion; R4 extensions would be mitigations, not base R6 alternatives.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The finding describes R6-only optional content and reverse-conversion risk. It does not identify a base R6 design choice that invalidates R4 instances moving forward, so `backwardCompatibleAlternativeAvailable` should not be `No` or `Yes`; the calibration is not applicable to a forward breaking-design alternative.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: For R6-to-R4 workflows, implementers may need standard or local R4 extensions, companion-resource mappings, or lossy conversion policy. Those are backport and migration mitigations rather than less-breaking R6 base designs. The optional additions themselves can coexist with all R4-valid forward-migrated instances.
